regime: Risk-off rotation. Stocks gapped to fresh highs overnight then reversed and sold off through the US session, flipping both index trend stops to short (NQ -0.75%, ES -0.21%). Soft jobs data was the trigger. Money rotated into safety: gold surged +4.19% and silver +4.30%. The VIX eased to 15.81 even as stocks dipped, so this read as an orderly rotation off stretched highs, not a fear spike.
summary: Risk rotation day. Stocks gapped to fresh highs overnight, with NQ tagging 30,073 to clear the 30,000 round number, then reversed and sold off through the US session. Both index trend stops flipped short: NQ closed -0.75% at 29,594.75 and ES -0.21% at 7,758.5. The driver was soft data. ADP private payrolls rose just 44,000 for July, well under the roughly 70,000 expected and the weakest in six months, and ISM Services showed its employment piece back in contraction. Money rotated into safety: gold surged +4.19% (MGC2! to 4,276, spot gold about +4%) and silver +4.30%, while crude sat flat and based near 75. One tell worth noting: the VIX eased to 15.81 even as stocks slipped, so this read as an orderly rotation off stretched highs, not a fear spike.
psychology: Yesterday the temptation was to chase strength into 30,000. Overnight, price tagged it (30,073) and then reversed, which is the classic trap: a round number after a big run is where breakouts most often fail. Today the temptation flips to the other extreme, gold up about 4% in a session. The fear of missing that move is the same chase risk, just pointed a different way. The skill both days is the same: wait for location. With gold, that means a pullback toward the 4,236 stop, not a market buy at 4,276. With the indices, it means a rally that fails under the flipped stop, not shorting the low after price already fell 500 points. And notice the calm VIX. The pullback was orderly, so there is no need to over-trade the downside either. Let price come to your level.

event.name: Soft jobs data: ADP employment and ISM Services
event.consensus: ADP private payrolls were expected around +70,000; ISM Services was expected near 54.5.
event.actual: ADP came in at just +44,000 for July, the weakest in six months, and ISM Services printed 54.1 with its employment component back in contraction at 47.4.
event.surprise: A clear downside miss on jobs. Soft labor data plus easing inflation expectations pulled money out of stretched tech and index highs and into safe havens.
event.nqReaction: NQ had tagged a fresh overnight high at 30,073 (clearing the 30,000 round number) then reversed through the US session to close 29,594.75 (-0.75%). ES did the same, closing 7,758.5 (-0.21%). Both index trend stops flipped short.
event.crossAsset: Gold MGC2! +4.19% (spot gold +4.04% to 4,246.64), silver +4.30% (62.04), the VIX eased to 15.81 (-4.18%), the 10-year yield sat near 4.639, and crude was flat at 75.05 (-0.11%).

risk.sizing: Volatility eased even though stocks slipped: the VIX fell to 15.81 (-4.18%) and NQ's ATR came down to 112.21 (from 121.86), so risk per contract is a touch smaller than yesterday. The trend flipped, so treat the new index shorts as day-one signals, not an established downtrend. Gold is the opposite problem: it is up about 4% and extended, so chasing 4,276 has poor location. A better with-trend gold entry is a pullback toward the 4,236 stop.
risk.openRisk: Both indices are now short below their stops (NQ 29,875, ES 7,790). Gold is long above 4,236. Crude is short below 76.95 but basing in a range. Keep each market as its own risk book; a gold long does not offset an index short.
risk.note: Week ahead: jobless claims Thursday, then the July jobs report Friday Aug 7, the highest-impact release of the week. Check your prop-firm blackout rules around each. Watch whether the indices keep closing below their flipped stops (confirming the pullback) or reclaim them (repairing the uptrend), and whether gold can hold its new highs.

Score: 5 rows, 5 triggered, 3 played out, 2 mixed, 0 failed. A genuine reversal day: both index breakouts tagged their first upside targets overnight then failed and flipped short, while the paired pullback branch, the gold long, and the crude short all played out. Best lesson: when a round number gets tagged after a big run, the breakout is often the trap and the reversal is the trade. Month to date (August): 15 rows, 11 triggered, 8 played out, 2 mixed, 0 failed.
